Williams board approval of Geismar ethylene expansion; Tier 2.

Dow SEC filing announced ~$4bn five-year investment program explicitly including construction of a 600 ktpa U.S. Gulf Coast PE plant; Tier 2.
BASF announced evaluation of a world-scale methane-to-propylene complex on the U.S. Gulf Coast.
BASF selected Freeport, specified ~475 ktpa capacity, contracted Air Liquide for basic engineering, and stated final board approval was still required in 2016.
BASF explicitly postponed its final investment decision because of raw-material price volatility and the prevailing economic environment.
Ascend selected UOP Oleflex technology for a >1 Mtpa on-purpose propylene project at Chocolate Bayou and stated it was taking development steps.
ICIS reports Ascend shelved the planned ~1 Mtpa Chocolate Bayou PDH project in Feb 2016 as the propylene/propane spread declined substantially; later CEO comments said revival was unlikely.
REXtac announced an integrated Odessa PDH/PP project including a 300 ktpa propylene unit.
ICIS reported that REXtac had cancelled its west-Texas PDH plan. The row date is the first source-locked public confirmation identified in this pass, not necessarily the private decision date.

LyondellBasell stated that detailed engineering was in process and long-lead items had already been ordered for the 800+ million lb/yr La Porte ethylene debottleneck; the same update gave a defined capital project and completion schedule. Ordering long-lead equipment is treated as an equivalent binding capital commitment, not as a permit or later construction inference.

LyondellBasell stated that detailed engineering had been contracted and long-lead items ordered for the Channelview methanol restart, with an approximately $150m capital cost and defined restart schedule. This is treated as equivalent binding capital commitment.

LyondellBasell reported that the Channelview expansion furnaces had been ordered and foundations poured, with mechanical completion scheduled. The date is the first source-locked observation of project-specific equipment procurement; procurement is used as equivalent binding capital commitment.

Dow SEC filing records the August 27, 2013 location decision and states that the ELITE polymer production unit will be built in Freeport as one of four announced U.S. Gulf Coast Performance Plastics investments. This is treated consistently with existing Tier-2 capital-investment announcement precedents.

Louisiana Economic Development and Dow announced a $1.06bn Plaquemine investment package including a new high-performance polyethylene plant and stated construction of the new polyolefins plants would begin by year-end 2013. The quantified company investment decision is treated as Tier-2 binding capital commitment.

Westlake SEC filing states that in April 2011 the company announced an expansion program to increase ethylene capacity of both Petro 1 and Petro 2; it further documents that 2011-2012 capital expenditures largely related to Petro 2. The program announcement plus contemporaneous capital spending supports Tier-2 commitment for Petro 2.

Westlake SEC filing states that in April 2011 it announced an expansion program covering both Lake Charles ethylene units, including Petro 1. The later filing documents substantial project costs already incurred before physical execution. Consistent with the existing Westlake Tier-2 announcement precedent, April 2011 is retained as the source-locked commitment month.

Chevron Phillips Chemical announced that it will expand Sweeny ethylene production by adding a tenth furnace, reported TCEQ consent to begin construction, and scheduled construction for the next quarter. The definitive company decision and immediately authorized execution are treated as Tier-2 commitment.

Formosa Plastics corporate history states that in 2014 its Board of Directors agreed to establish Formosa Industries Corporation in the U.S. to invest in a 1.2 Mt/y ethane cracker and a 400 kt/y HDPE plant. The board action directly satisfies Tier 2; only year precision is recoverable from the source.

V14 recovery safety-margin audit: Dow's Q1 2012 Form 10-Q, filed 2012-05-02, describes the St. Charles ethylene cracker restart as the first project in a set of announced U.S. Gulf Coast investments, with completion expected by year-end 2012. To avoid back-dating the commitment to the preliminary April 2011 'finalizing plans' announcement, v14 uses the SEC filing date as the first source-locked public Tier-2 confirmation of the capital investment. This is not inferred from the later restart/startup date.
